 Looking for balance in midfield published at 12:33 GMT 12:33 GMT 
 Man City 0-0 Fulham 
 Shamoon Hafez 
Football reporter at Etihad Stadium 
 Manchester City boss Enzo Maresca spoke on Friday about needing to find the right "balance" in his squad and it means the £125m man Enzo Fernandez has been dropped for this game.
 Elliot Anderson and Ayyoub Bouaddi are holding the fort this lunchtime, can it provide a more secure base for the hosts?
 9 6 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 'Players will have been stewing over it' published at 12:32 GMT 12:32 GMT 
 Man City 0-0 Fulham 
 Joe Cole 
Former Chelsea and England midfielder on TNT Sports 
 These games when you come back from a break, Man City won't have had many players in the building. 
 But those that were still here will have been stewing over their last defeat. 
 Fulham will want to test the midfield fragility we've seen in the past few games.

 'Slightly better balance in midfield' published at 12:25 GMT 12:25 GMT 
 Man City v Fulham (12:30 GMT) 
 Alan Shearer 
Former England striker on BBC Radio 5 Live 
 Image source, Getty Images Even when Manchester City were winning games, I think there was a slight concern that they were too easy to play through, lack of protection in front of the back four.
 Too many mistakes from individuals and they've been punished so that's why Enzo Maresca has changed it up today.
 I do think there is a sightly better balance in the midfield today with [Elliot] Anderson and [Ayyoub] Bouaddi because both Anderson and [Enzo] Fernandez like to get forward.

 'They're important players' published at 12:20 GMT 12:20 GMT 
 Man City v Fulham (12:30 GMT) 
 Manchester City 
 Enzo Maresca has just spoken to TNT Sports. 
 On a reaction coming back after the international break: "It's not about reaction it's about doing the right things to win the game on and off the ball."
 On today's squad changes: "I don't think it's a matter of balance, with Fernandes we won seven games in a row. I just think for this game it's better having Bouaddi in there."
 On having Khusanov and Bouaddi starting today: "They're important, very both important players for us, for defending and being aggressive."
 On goalkeeper Donnarumma's recent mistakes: "It's for all the players when you make a mistake, it's normal to want to stop that and Donnarumma is going to stop that."
 On how important is today's game for the table: "All matches are important. The next 28 are all important."

 A rare run published at 12:18 GMT 12:18 GMT

 Manchester City have lost each of their past three Premier League games, as many as in their previous 36 (W25 D8); since the start of 2007-08, they’ve only lost four in a row twice, doing so in August 2008 and December 2024.

 Man City v Fulham (12:30 GMT)

Former Chelsea and England midfielder on TNT Sports 
 On Phil Foden starting: "If I was on the coaching staff, I would have started the process early this week telling him how good he is. 
 "He knows himself and he has to be Phil Foden, he has to be the player that makes the difference.
